out_of_scope_touched.why: Not in the prompt's named file list. Added headPinned: true / footPinned: true to the `guests` route's data. RouteChromeData is declared to gain these fields (acceptance bullet 5) and private-layout is built to read them (bullet 8), but nothing in the named scope ever sets them to true on a real route — without this, the whole pinning mechanism this task ships would have no production consumer, and the moved guest-manager pinning-contract test (bullet 3) would only be provable against a synthetic test-only route rather than the real `guests` route guest-manager actually serves. Judged necessary to satisfy the acceptance bullets' evident intent; flagged here per the skill's §3 rather than made silently.

risks.risk: guest-manager's scroll-triggered auto-grow (onListScroll, bound to .table-body's own (scroll) event) and its scroll-to-top-on-filter/search/sort (resetWindow, writing .table-body's scrollTop) both become dead code in a real browser once .table-body sheds overflow-y:auto (this task's own acceptance bullet 10) — .table-body no longer scrolls, so its scroll event never fires and its scrollTop is never non-zero. The real scrolling element is now PrivateLayout's .screen-scroll, which lives outside GuestManager's own template with no channel back to it. guest-manager.spec.ts's scroll tests keep passing because they dispatch synthetic scroll events directly on .table-body with mocked geometry, which JSDOM never exercises via real layout — so the test suite cannot see this regression. The manual 'Load more' button is unaffected. Documented at both call sites in guest-manager.ts; not fixed here because a correct fix (e.g. an IntersectionObserver-based trigger, or a cross-layer channel to .screen-scroll) is a design decision beyond this task's named scope, and I could not verify any fix in a real browser.
risks.surfaces_at: T343 (when the other three oversized screens migrate and may hit the same class of gap) or the first real-device QA pass on /guests after this ships — nearing the bottom of a long guest list will silently stop auto-loading the next page, and changing a filter/search/sort while scrolled down will silently leave the view mid-list instead of jumping to the top

risks.risk: The desktop .table-header/.table-row alignment fix (calc(#{t.$space-6} + 16px) padding on .table-header, replacing the outer gutter .table-container used to supply) is a reasoned, token-only calculation but was never visually verified — no browser tool available. If the arithmetic is off, column labels would sit slightly misaligned above their cells at >=900px only (mobile is unaffected, .table-header is display:none there).
risks.surfaces_at: First real-browser or screenshot-based review of /guests at desktop width
